blog_post.body_html:
Understanding Coffee Processing in India

Before your morning cup reaches your mug, the coffee beans undergo one of two main drying processes: agglomeration or freeze-drying. Agglomerated coffee uses hot air to dry coffee extracts, which can sometimes degrade delicate aromatic compounds and leave room for cheap fillers like chicory. On the other hand, freeze-drying locks in the authentic aroma and rich taste by freezing the coffee extract at extremely low temperatures and removing water through sublimation.

Why Purity Beans Chooses Zero Chicory

Many commercial brands in India bulk up their agglomerated powders with chicory root, masking the true taste of coffee. Purity Beans rejects this completely. Every jar of Purity Beans contains 100% pure coffee with zero chicory and no hidden ingredients. When you compare freeze dried vs agglomerated coffee, the real test is what is left out of the jar. By keeping our coffee 100% pure, Purity Beans ensures you never compromise on taste or transparency.

Cost vs Quality: The Rs 18 Reality

Paying Rs 180 at a cafe for a diluted brew no longer makes sense when you can brew a superior cup at home for just Rs 18 per serving. Purity Beans delivers gourmet instant coffee quality straight to your kitchen without cafe markups or mystery fillers.
